construction.implementation_origin: Original isolated reference implementation with clearly labeled synthetic fixtures

input.dataset_label: nonblank string; example is explicitly SYNTHETIC

config.categories: nonempty ordered array of {id, keywords, base_priority, team, owner}; unique IDs
config.priority_rules: ordered array of {keywords, priority}; nonempty keyword arrays

input.tickets: array of {id, subject, body}; unique nonblank IDs, text may be empty

output.results: ordered array of {ticket_id, category, priority, route: {team, owner}, reason}

shared_schema.validation: One validate() boundary used by triage() and the CLI. Exact fields and types, unique IDs, recognized priorities, accountable routes, valid fallback, no blank or case-insensitive duplicate keywords. At most 10000 tickets, 1000 categories/rules/keywords per array, 100000 characters per string. Duplicate JSON keys and non-finite constants rejected.
shared_schema.errors: CLI prints one JSON object {status: error, error: message} and exits 2 for usage, file, decoding, JSON or validation errors; success exits 0.

cross_stage_handoffs: Single integrated functionality: validated ticket text -> first matching category or fallback -> maximum matching priority -> configured accountable team and owner -> shared JSON result.
behavior: Casefolded substring keyword matching across subject and body, separated by a newline; not semantic or whole-word matching.
Category configuration order resolves ambiguity; matching keyword evidence is returned.
Priority ordering is low < normal < high < urgent. Rules only raise a category baseline; all matched rules are recorded with zero-based indices.
Fallback categories can have keywords but need not. Every route has a nonblank team and accountable owner.
Empty batches are valid; empty ticket text uses fallback. Input order and values are preserved, input is not mutated.
No live model or optional callable is needed; all decisions are deterministic.

included: Configurable categorization, priority rules and accountable routing
Runnable CLI, synthetic example, standard-library tests
excluded: Live LLMs, networking, external integrations or providers
Model training, probabilistic inference or semantic classification
Ticket persistence, queue delivery, authentication and SLA scheduling
Enterprise production hardening, workload-aware assignment and human escalation workflows

test_outcomes.cli_example: passed: one JSON object, status ok, three routed tickets
